title: Male body: anterior anatomy
description: A glass-body view of the male: every major organ in place, from brain to testes, with the reproductive tract in the pelvis.

questions.question: Where are the main organs in the male body?
questions.answer: The brain is in the skull; lungs and heart occupy the chest; liver, stomach, intestines and kidneys occupy the abdomen; and pelvic organs include bladder and reproductive structures.

questions.question: Does a male body map show every deep structure?
questions.answer: No. The overview is an orientation map; its chapter links provide deeper tissue, vascular, skeletal and nerve details not separately visible on one full-body plate.

questions.question: Where is the brain shown on the male body map?
questions.answer: Control centre housed in the skull, glowing through the translucent scalp. Function: Integrates sensation, movement, thought, memory and autonomic drive.

questions.question: Where are the lungs in the male body map?
questions.answer: Paired thoracic organs flanking the heart. Function: Gas exchange across ~300 million alveoli.

questions.question: What does the liver do in the male body?
questions.answer: Function: Metabolism, detoxification, bile, plasma proteins. Largest internal organ, right upper quadrant.
